title: Chapter 3 — Cetacea
description: Fully aquatic mammals descended from land-dwelling artiodactyls, most closely related to hippos. About 90 living species divided into Mysticeti (baleen whales) and Odontoceti (toothed whales). The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever existed.

children.name: Balaena
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the bowhead whale, the only great whale that lives its entire life in Arctic and subarctic waters, distinguished by its massive arched jaw and ability to break through sea ice.

children.name: Balaena mysticetus
children.description: The bowhead whale (Balaena mysticetus), sometimes known as the Greenland right whale, Arctic whale, and polar whale, is a species of baleen whale belonging to the family Balaenidae and is the only living representative of the genus Balaena.

children.name: Eubalaena
children.description: Comprises 3 species of right whales found in the North Atlantic, North Pacific, and Southern Ocean, recognised by their rotund bodies, lack of a dorsal fin, and distinctive white callosities on the head.

children.name: Eubalaena glacialis
children.description: The North Atlantic right whale (Eubalaena glacialis) is a baleen whale, one of three right whale species belonging to the genus Eubalaena, all of which were formerly classified as a single species..

children.name: Eubalaena japonica
children.description: The North Pacific right whale (Eubalaena japonica) is a very large, thickset baleen whale species that is extremely rare and endangered..

children.name: Eubalaena australis
children.description: The southern right whale (Eubalaena australis) is a large baleen whale and one of three species of right whale belonging to the genus Eubalaena.

children.name: Caperea
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the pygmy right whale, the smallest and most enigmatic baleen whale, found only in cool temperate waters of the Southern Hemisphere.

children.name: Caperea marginata
children.description: The pygmy right whale (Caperea marginata) is a species of baleen whale.

children.name: Eschrichtius
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the gray whale, notable for its 20,000 km annual migrations between Arctic feeding grounds and subtropical breeding lagoons along the Pacific coast of North America and Asia.

children.name: Eschrichtius robustus
children.description: The gray whale, also known as the grey whale, is a baleen whale that migrates between feeding and breeding grounds yearly. It reaches a length of 14.9–15.2 m (49–50 ft), a weight of up to 41 to 45 tonnes and lives between 55 and 70 years, although one female was estimated to be 75–80 years of age. One of the longest-living gray whales currently is a female, first sighted in 1977, and estimated to be 53–55 years old as of 2024.

children.name: Balaenoptera
children.description: The largest rorqual genus with 8 species including the blue whale (the largest animal ever known), found in all world's oceans and united by their streamlined bodies and pleated throat pouches for lunge-feeding.

children.name: Balaenoptera musculus
children.description: The blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) is a species of baleen whale and the largest marine mammal in the rorqual family Balaenopteridae.

children.name: Balaenoptera physalus
children.description: The fin whale (Balaenoptera physalus), also known as the finback whale or common rorqual, is a species of baleen whale and the second-longest cetacean after the blue whale.

children.name: Balaenoptera borealis
children.description: The sei whale ( , ; Balaenoptera borealis) is a baleen whale.

children.name: Balaenoptera edeni
children.description: Bryde's whale  ( BRUU-dəz), or the Bryde's whale complex, putatively comprises three species of rorqual and possibly four..

children.name: Balaenoptera omurai
children.description: Omura's whale or the dwarf fin whale (Balaenoptera omurai) is a species of rorqual about which very little is known..

children.name: Balaenoptera ricei
children.description: Rice's whale (Balaenoptera ricei), also known as the Gulf of Mexico whale, is a species of baleen whale endemic to the northern Gulf of Mexico..

children.name: Balaenoptera acutorostrata
children.description: The common minke whale or northern minke whale (Balaenoptera acutorostrata) is a species of minke whale within the suborder of baleen whales.

children.name: Balaenoptera bonaerensis
children.description: The Antarctic minke whale or southern minke whale (Balaenoptera bonaerensis) is a species of minke whale within the suborder of baleen whales.

children.name: Megaptera
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the humpback whale, known worldwide for its complex songs, acrobatic breaching, and exceptionally long pectoral fins, inhabiting all oceans from the poles to the tropics.

children.name: Megaptera novaeangliae
children.description: The humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) is a species of baleen whale.

children.name: Physeter
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the sperm whale, the largest toothed predator on Earth, distinguished by its enormous squarish head housing the spermaceti organ, and capable of diving over 2 km to hunt deep-sea squid.

children.name: Physeter macrocephalus
children.description: The sperm whale or cachalot (Physeter macrocephalus) is the largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator.

children.name: Kogia
children.description: Contains 2 small, little-known species (pygmy and dwarf sperm whales) found in tropical to temperate offshore waters worldwide, notable for their shark-like false gill markings and ability to eject a cloud of reddish feces as a defence.

children.name: Kogia breviceps
children.description: The pygmy sperm whale (Kogia breviceps) is one of two extant species in the family Kogiidae in the sperm whale superfamily.

children.name: Kogia sima
children.description: The dwarf sperm whale is a sperm whale that inhabits temperate and tropical oceans worldwide, in particular continental shelves and slopes. It was first described by biologist Richard Owen in 1866, based on illustrations by naturalist Sir Walter Elliot. The species was considered to be synonymous with the pygmy sperm whale from 1878 until 1998.

children.name: Delphinapterus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the beluga, an Arctic and subarctic whale uniquely lacking a dorsal fin, with a flexible melon and exceptional vocal range that earned it the nickname 'canary of the sea.'

children.name: Delphinapterus leucas
children.description: The beluga whale (; Delphinapterus leucas), is an Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean.

children.name: Monodon
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the narwhal, an Arctic cetacean in which males bear a spiralled ivory tusk that can reach 3 m and is now known to function as a sensory organ, living year-round in pack ice.

children.name: Monodon monoceros
children.description: The narwhal (Monodon monoceros) is a species of toothed whale native to the Arctic.

children.name: Berardius
children.description: Contains 2 species of giant beaked whales in the North Pacific — the largest beaked whales, reaching up to 13 m — known for deep diving and small triangular teeth at the tip of the lower jaw.

children.name: Berardius bairdii
children.description: Baird's beaked whale (Berardius bairdii), also known commonly as the northern giant bottlenose whale, North Pacific bottlenose whale, giant four-toothed whale, northern four-toothed whale and North Pacific four-toothed whale, is a species of whale in the genus Berardius of the family Ziphiidae..

children.name: Berardius minimus
children.description: Sato's beaked whale (Berardius minimus; Japanese: Kurotsuchi-kujira) is a little-known species of four-toothed whale, a type of beaked whale..

children.name: Hyperoodon
children.description: Contains 2 species of bottlenose whales (northern and southern) distinguished by their bulbous foreheads and affinity for deep cold waters, with the northern species historically hunted commercially by the Norwegians.

children.name: Hyperoodon ampullatus
children.description: The northern bottlenose whale (Hyperoodon ampullatus) is a species of beaked whale in the ziphiid family, being one of two members of the genus Hyperoodon.

children.name: Hyperoodon planifrons
children.description: The southern bottlenose whale (Hyperoodon planifrons) is a species of whale, in the ziphiid family, one of two members of the genus Hyperoodon..

children.name: Indopacetus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Longman's beaked whale, one of the least-known cetaceans, found in tropical and warm temperate waters of the Indo-Pacific and recognised from relatively few confirmed sightings.

children.name: Indopacetus pacificus
children.description: The tropical bottlenose whale, also known as the Indo-Pacific beaked whale or Longman's beaked whale, is a species of beaked whale in the family Ziphiidae. It is the only species in the genus Indopacetus. Known as of 2010 known from about a dozen strandings and over 65 sightings, it was considered to be the world's rarest cetacean until recently, but the spade-toothed whale now holds that position.

children.name: Mesoplodon
children.description: The largest beaked whale genus with 14 species distributed across all ocean basins, characterised by males bearing a single pair of large teeth erupting from the mid-lower jaw, with many species known only from strandings.

children.name: Mesoplodon bidens
children.description: Sowerby's beaked whale (Mesoplodon bidens), also known as the North Atlantic or North Sea beaked whale, is a species of toothed whale..

children.name: Mesoplodon densirostris
children.description: Blainville's beaked whale (Mesoplodon densirostris), or the dense-beaked whale, is believed to be the widest ranging mesoplodont whale..

children.name: Mesoplodon europaeus
children.description: Gervais's beaked whale (Mesoplodon europaeus), sometimes known as the Antillean beaked whale, Gulf Stream beaked whale, or European beaked whale (from which its scientific name is derived), is the most frequently stranding type of mesoplodont whale off the coast of North America..

children.name: Mesoplodon grayi
children.description: Gray's beaked whale (Mesoplodon grayi), sometimes known as Haast's beaked whale, the scamperdown whale, or the southern beaked whale, is one of the better-known members of the genus Mesoplodon..

children.name: Mesoplodon hectori
children.description: Hector's beaked whale (Mesoplodon hectori) is a small mesoplodont living in the Southern Hemisphere..

children.name: Mesoplodon layardii
children.description: The strap-toothed beaked whale (Mesoplodon layardii), also known as Layard's beaked whale, is one of the largest members of the Mesoplodon genus, growing to 6.2 m (20 ft) in length and reaching up to 1,300 kg (2,900 lb)..

children.name: Mesoplodon mirus
children.description: True's beaked whale (Mesoplodon mirus) is a medium-sized whale in the genus Mesoplodon..

children.name: Mesoplodon peruvianus
children.description: The pygmy beaked whale (Mesoplodon peruvianus), also known as the bandolero beaked whale, Peruvian beaked whale and lesser beaked whale, is the smallest of the mesoplodonts and one of the newest discoveries.

children.name: Mesoplodon stejnegeri
children.description: Stejneger's beaked whale (Mesoplodon stejnegeri), also known as the Bering Sea beaked whale or the saber-toothed whale, is a relatively unknown member of the genus Mesoplodon inhabiting the North Pacific Ocean..

children.name: Mesoplodon bowdoini
children.description: Andrews' beaked whale (Mesoplodon bowdoini), sometimes known as the deep-crest beaked whale or splay-toothed whale, is one of the least known members of a poorly known genus..

children.name: Mesoplodon carlhubbsi
children.description: Hubbs' beaked whale (Mesoplodon carlhubbsi) was initially thought to be an Andrews' beaked whale when discovered by ichthyologist Carl Hubbs; however, it was named in his honor when it was discovered to be a new species..

children.name: Mesoplodon ginkgodens
children.description: The ginkgo-toothed beaked whale (Mesoplodon ginkgodens) is a poorly known species of beaked whale named for the unusual shape of its dual teeth..

children.name: Mesoplodon traversii
children.description: The spade-toothed whale (Mesoplodon traversii) is the rarest species of beaked whale..

children.name: Mesoplodon hotaula
children.description: Deraniyagala's beaked whale (Mesoplodon hotaula) is a species of mesoplodont whale closely related to the ginkgo-toothed beaked whale..

children.name: Ziphius
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Cuvier's beaked whale, the world's deepest and longest-diving mammal (exceeding 2,992 m and 137 minutes on a single breath), found in deep waters across all oceans.

children.name: Ziphius cavirostris
children.description: Cuvier's beaked whale, goose-beaked whale, or ziphius (Ziphius cavirostris) is the most widely distributed of all beaked whales in the family Ziphiidae..

children.name: Tasmacetus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Shepherd's beaked whale, unique among beaked whales in retaining a full set of functional teeth in both jaws, found in cool temperate Southern Hemisphere waters.

children.name: Tasmacetus shepherdi
children.description: Shepherd's beaked whale (Tasmacetus shepherdi), also commonly called Tasman's beaked whale or simply the Tasman whale, is a cetacean of the family Ziphiidae and the only species in the genus Tasmacetus..

children.name: Delphinus
children.description: Contains 2 species of common dolphins with a distinctive hourglass pattern on their flanks, forming some of the largest dolphin schools on Earth in warm-temperate and tropical waters worldwide.

children.name: Delphinus delphis
children.description: The common dolphin (Delphinus delphis) is the most abundant cetacean in the world, with an estimated global population of about six million.

children.name: Delphinus capensis
children.description: The common dolphin (Delphinus delphis) is the most abundant cetacean in the world, with an estimated global population of about six million.

children.name: Tursiops
children.description: Contains 2 species of bottlenose dolphins — the most extensively studied cetaceans — found in coastal and oceanic waters worldwide, known for high intelligence, complex social bonds, and tool use.

children.name: Tursiops truncatus
children.description: The common bottlenose dolphin or Atlantic bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) is one of three species of bottlenose dolphin in the genus Tursiops.

children.name: Tursiops aduncus
children.description: The Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops aduncus) is a species of bottlenose dolphin..

children.name: Orcinus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the killer whale (orca), the largest member of the dolphin family and apex predator of all oceans, notable for its ecotypes, cooperative hunting strategies, and complex cultural traditions.

children.name: Orcinus orca
children.description: The orca (Orcinus orca), or killer whale, is a toothed whale and the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family.

children.name: Globicephala
children.description: Contains 2 species of pilot whales — large, bulbous-headed social dolphins that travel in tight pods — found in deep offshore waters globally and infamous for mass strandings.

children.name: Globicephala melas
children.description: The long-finned pilot whale or pothead whale (Globicephala melas) is a large species of oceanic dolphin..

children.name: Globicephala macrorhynchus
children.description: The short-finned pilot whale (Globicephala macrorhynchus) is one of the two species of cetaceans in the genus Globicephala, which it shares with the long-finned pilot whale (G..

children.name: Grampus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Risso's dolphin, a blunt-headed, heavily scarred species found in deep temperate and tropical waters worldwide that feeds almost exclusively on squid.

children.name: Grampus griseus
children.description: Risso's dolphin (Grampus griseus) is the only species of the genus Grampus in the family Delphinidae (dolphins)..

children.name: Pseudorca
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the false killer whale, a large, slender, uniformly dark dolphin found in tropical and subtropical seas worldwide known for sharing prey with other dolphins and occasional fish depredation.

children.name: Pseudorca crassidens
children.description: The false killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens) is a species of oceanic dolphin that is the only extant representative of the genus Pseudorca.

children.name: Orcaella
children.description: Contains 2 species of stocky, snub-nosed dolphins — the Irrawaddy dolphin of Southeast Asian rivers and coasts, and the Australian snubfin dolphin — notable for their round heads and lack of a prominent beak.

children.name: Orcaella brevirostris
children.description: The Irrawaddy dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris) is a euryhaline species of oceanic dolphin found in scattered subpopulations near sea coasts and in estuaries and rivers in parts of the Bay of Bengal and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Orcaella heinsohni
children.description: The Australian snubfin dolphin (Orcaella heinsohni) is a dolphin found off the northern coasts of Australia..

children.name: Sousa
children.description: Contains 4 species of humpback dolphins inhabiting shallow coastal and estuarine waters of the Indian and western Pacific Oceans and West Africa, named for the dorsal hump that carries a small fin in some species.

children.name: Sousa chinensis
children.description: The Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin (Sousa chinensis) is a species of humpback dolphin inhabiting coastal waters of the eastern Indian and western Pacific Oceans..

children.name: Sousa sahulensis
children.description: The Australian humpback dolphin (Sousa sahulensis) is a species of humpback dolphin and the fourth recognized humpback dolphin species chronologically..

children.name: Sousa plumbea
children.description: The Indian Ocean humpback dolphin (Sousa plumbea) is a member of the Delphinidae family occupying coastal areas ranging from Southern Africa to Western Indochina..

children.name: Sousa taiwanensis
children.description: Sousa taiwanensis (Chinese white dolphin) is a dolphins species found in Asia region.

children.name: Stenella
children.description: Contains 5 species of small, slender oceanic dolphins — including spinner and spotted dolphins — widespread in tropical and warm-temperate seas and infamous for by-catch mortality in tuna purse-seine fisheries.

children.name: Stenella attenuata
children.description: The pantropical spotted dolphin is a species of dolphin found in all the world's temperate and tropical oceans. The species was beginning to come under threat due to the killing of millions of individuals in tuna purse seines. In the 1980s, the rise of "dolphin-friendly" tuna capture methods saved millions of the species in the eastern Pacific Ocean and it is now one of the most abundant dolphin species in the world.

children.name: Stenella longirostris
children.description: The spinner dolphin (Stenella longirostris) is a small dolphin found in off-shore tropical waters around the world.

children.name: Stenella clymene
children.description: The Clymene dolphin (Stenella clymene), in older texts known as the short-snouted spinner dolphin, is a dolphin endemic to the Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Stenella coeruleoalba
children.description: The striped dolphin (Stenella coeruleoalba) is a dolphin found in temperate and tropical waters of all the world's oceans.

children.name: Stenella frontalis
children.description: The Atlantic spotted dolphin (Stenella frontalis) is a dolphin found in warm temperate and tropical waters of the Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Steno
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the rough-toothed dolphin, a warm-water offshore species found across all tropical and subtropical oceans, distinguishable by its narrow, elongated head with a gradually sloping forehead and wrinkled teeth.

children.name: Steno bredanensis
children.description: The rough-toothed dolphin (Steno bredanensis) is a species of dolphin that lives in deep warm and tropical waters around the world..

children.name: Lagenodelphis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Fraser's dolphin, a robust, short-beaked oceanic species of tropical and subtropical waters that travels in dense, cohesive schools and was not formally described until 1956.

children.name: Lagenodelphis hosei
children.description: Fraser's dolphin or the Sarawak dolphin (Lagenodelphis hosei) is a cetacean in the family Delphinidae found in deep waters in the Pacific Ocean and to a lesser extent in the Indian and Atlantic Oceans..

children.name: Lagenorhynchus
children.description: Contains 6 species of fast-swimming, short-beaked dolphins (including white-sided and dusky dolphins) ranging from cold temperate to subpolar waters of both hemispheres, often seen bow-riding and breaching.

children.name: Lagenorhynchus acutus
children.description: The Atlantic white-sided dolphin (Leucopleurus acutus) is a distinctively coloured dolphin found in the cool to temperate waters of the North Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Lagenorhynchus albirostris
children.description: The white-beaked dolphin (Lagenorhynchus albirostris) is a marine mammal belonging to the family Delphinidae (oceanic dolphins) in the suborder Odontoceti (toothed whales)..

children.name: Lagenorhynchus australis
children.description: Peale's dolphin (Cephalorhynchus australis) is a small dolphin found in the waters around Tierra del Fuego at the foot of South America..

children.name: Lagenorhynchus cruciger
children.description: The hourglass dolphin (Cephalorhynchus cruciger) is a small dolphin in the family Delphinidae that inhabits offshore Antarctic and sub-Antarctic waters.

children.name: Lagenorhynchus obliquidens
children.description: The Pacific white-sided dolphin (Aethalodelphis obliquidens), also known as the hookfin porpoise, is an active dolphin found in the cool or temperate waters of the North Pacific Ocean.

children.name: Lagenorhynchus obscurus
children.description: The dusky dolphin (Aethalodelphis obscurus) is a small oceanic dolphin found in coastal waters of the Southern Hemisphere.

children.name: Lissodelphis
children.description: Contains 2 species of sleek, dorsally finless dolphins — one in the North Pacific and one in the Southern Ocean — characterised by their streamlined black-and-white bodies and high-speed swimming.

children.name: Lissodelphis borealis
children.description: The northern right whale dolphin (Lissodelphis borealis) is a small, slender species of cetacean found in the cold and temperate waters of the North Pacific Ocean.

children.name: Lissodelphis peronii
children.description: The southern right whale dolphin (Lissodelphis peronii) is a small and slender species of cetacean, found in cool waters of the Southern Hemisphere.

children.name: Cephalorhynchus
children.description: Contains 4 species of small, stocky coastal dolphins (including Commerson's and Hector's dolphins) restricted to cold temperate waters of the Southern Hemisphere, with rounded dorsal fins and striking black-and-white patterns.

children.name: Cephalorhynchus commersonii
children.description: Commerson's dolphin (Cephalorhynchus commersonii) is also referred to by the common names jacobita, skunk dolphin, piebald dolphin, panda dolphin, or tonina overa (in South America)..

children.name: Cephalorhynchus eutropia
children.description: The Chilean dolphin (Cephalorhynchus eutropia), also known as the Black dolphin, is one of six dolphins in the genus Cephalorhynchus.

children.name: Cephalorhynchus heavisidii
children.description: Heaviside's dolphin (Cephalorhynchus heavisidii) is one of six dolphins in the genus Cephalorhynchus..

children.name: Cephalorhynchus hectori
children.description: Hector's dolphin (Cephalorhynchus hectori) is one of six dolphin species belonging to the genus Cephalorhynchus..

children.name: Feresa
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the pygmy killer whale, a small, rarely seen tropical offshore dolphin known for its aggression toward other cetaceans despite its modest size of around 2.5 m.

children.name: Feresa attenuata
children.description: The pygmy killer whale (Feresa attenuata) is a poorly known and rarely seen oceanic dolphin.

children.name: Peponocephala
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the melon-headed whale, a small, gregarious tropical dolphin that congregates in schools of hundreds to thousands in deep offshore waters across the Indo-Pacific and Atlantic.

children.name: Peponocephala electra
children.description: The melon-headed whale (Peponocephala electra), also known less commonly as the electra dolphin, little killer whale, or many-toothed blackfish, is a toothed whale of the oceanic dolphin family (Delphinidae)..

children.name: Sotalia
children.description: Contains 2 small South American dolphin species — the tucuxi of Amazonian rivers and the costero of coastal waters — among the few delphinids to inhabit freshwater, with compact builds and subtle blue-grey colouration.

children.name: Sotalia fluviatilis
children.description: The tucuxi (Sotalia fluviatilis), alternatively known in Peru bufeo gris or bufeo negro, is a species of freshwater dolphin found in the rivers of the Amazon basin..

children.name: Sotalia guianensis
children.description: thumb|Sound of Sotalia guianensis The Guiana dolphin (Sotalia guianensis), also known as the estuarine dolphin or costero, is a dolphin found in the coastal and estuary waters to the north and east of South America, and east of Central America.

children.name: Phocoena
children.description: Contains 4 porpoise species including the harbour porpoise of North Atlantic and Pacific coasts and the critically endangered vaquita of the Gulf of California, all small and shy with spade-shaped teeth.

children.name: Phocoena phocoena
children.description: The harbour porpoise (Phocoena phocoena) is one of eight extant species of porpoise.

children.name: Phocoena spinipinnis
children.description: Burmeister's porpoise (Phocoena spinipinnis) is a species of porpoise endemic to the coast of South America..

children.name: Phocoena sinus
children.description: The vaquita ( və-KEE-tə; Phocoena sinus)  is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico..

children.name: Phocoena dioptrica
children.description: The spectacled porpoise (Phocoena dioptrica) is a small to midsize porpoise indigenous to the Southern Ocean.

children.name: Phocoenoides
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Dall's porpoise, the fastest small cetacean reaching up to 55 km/h, found in cold-temperate to subarctic waters of the North Pacific and identified by its bold black-and-white markings.

children.name: Phocoenoides dalli
children.description: Dall's porpoise (Phocoenoides dalli) is a species of porpoise endemic to the North Pacific..

children.name: Neophocaena
children.description: Contains 2 species of finless porpoises inhabiting shallow coastal and riverine waters from the Persian Gulf to Japan, the only porpoises without a dorsal fin, with a ridge of tubercles along the back instead.

children.name: Neophocaena asiaeorientalis
children.description: The Yangtze finless porpoise (Neophocaena asiaeorientalis) is a species of toothed whale in the family Phocoenidae, the porpoise family..

children.name: Neophocaena phocaenoides
children.description: The Indo-Pacific finless porpoise (Neophocaena phocaenoides) is one of eight porpoise species..

children.name: Platanista
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the South Asian river dolphin, found in the Ganges and Indus river systems, functionally blind with vestigial eyes and relying entirely on echolocation to navigate turbid waters.

children.name: Platanista gangetica
children.description: The Ganges river dolphin (Platanista gangetica) is a freshwater dolphin in the family Platanistidae.

children.name: Inia
children.description: Contains 3 species of Amazon river dolphins (botos), the largest river dolphins, found in the Amazon and Orinoco basins and recognisable by their pink colouration, flexible necks, and long beaks adapted for foraging on floodplain floors.

children.name: Inia geoffrensis
children.description: The Amazon river dolphin (Inia geoffrensis), also known as the boto, bufeo or pink river dolphin, is a species of toothed whale endemic to South America and is classified in the family Iniidae.

children.name: Inia boliviensis
children.description: The Bolivian river dolphin is a species (Inia boliviensis) or subspecies (Inia geoffrensis boliviensis) of freshwater dolphin found in upstream areas of the Amazon Basin..

children.name: Inia araguaiaensis
children.description: The Araguaian river dolphin  or Araguaian boto (Inia araguaiaensis) is a South American river dolphin population native to the Araguaia–Tocantins basin of Brazil..

children.name: Pontoporia
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the La Plata dolphin (franciscana), the only river dolphin found primarily in coastal marine and estuarine waters of southeastern South America, with one of the longest beaks relative to body size of any cetacean.

children.name: Pontoporia blainvillei
children.description: The La Plata dolphin, franciscana or toninha (Pontoporia blainvillei) is a species of river dolphin found in coastal Atlantic waters of southeastern South America..

children.name: Lipotes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the baiji, a functionally extinct Yangtze river dolphin last confirmed sighted in 2002, representing the first cetacean driven to extinction by human activity.

children.name: Lipotes vexillifer
children.description: The baiji (Lipotes vexillifer) is a possibly extinct species of river dolphin native to the Yangtze river system in China..
